title: Caltech and AIM Build AI Platform with Mathematicians for Mathematicians
source_used: Caltech (official university news release, read in full)
key_facts: Caltech and the American Institute of Mathematics (AIM) are building an AI software platform designed with mathematicians for mathematicians.
AIM has been housed on the Caltech campus since 2023; the platform is a collaboration between AIM and Caltech's Information Science and Technology initiative (IST).

The platform is meant to organise and connect mathematical work: it can suggest connections, conjectures and strategies, pursue several lines of reasoning in parallel, and show how competing approaches evolve.
The team began the work about nine months ago: Sergei Gukov (executive director of AIM), Yisong Yue (professor of computing and mathematical sciences) and Pietro Perona (director of IST).
A preliminary platform is due to be running in a few months for teams of mathematicians to test; AIM welcomes more than 1,000 visiting mathematicians a year.
The team expects about a year of user data before a radical redesign, which would include training a new AI system; it is still looking for major sources of support.
The platform will integrate conversion of human mathematical reasoning into Lean code, a language that computers can check, because current LLMs are inefficient at it.
quote_evidence: I think the community is really craving something that is not just all AI or no AI.
Within a year, we expect to have sufficient data to help us better understand how mathematicians use the platform.
We are looking for major sources of support to make that work possible.
why_it_matters_hint: A university-led attempt to give mathematicians an AI tool that they design and share, at a time when the field is divided over AI.
notes: Full text read (7k chars). Official Caltech release, so the announcement is confirmed; the capabilities are the team's plans, with no results yet. Two donors named in the text (Paul Stahura, Rahim Noorani) have no position given in the text, so they are not named in the entry.
